column1: # path-map.tsv — where the workspace lives on each machine.
# TAB-separated:  COMPUTER-NAME <TAB> WORKSPACE-ROOT
# COMPUTER-NAME is this machine's name, or "*" for the default. It is resolved as
# `scutil --get ComputerName` on macOS, falling back to `hostname -s` on Linux and
# WSL2 — run whichever applies and copy the answer exactly. First an exact match,
# then "*", then $HOME/dev. $CLAUDE_WORKSPACE_ROOT overrides everything. $HOME and
# a leading ~ are expanded.
# PUT A CUSTOM ROOT ON A MACHINE-NAME ROW, NEVER ON "*".
# This file syncs, so a "*" row naming one machine's custom location becomes every
# machine's — and a machine then hunts for its memory inside a path that belongs to
# a different computer. Rows whose directory does not exist here are skipped for
# exactly that reason, so the mistake degrades to "falls back to $HOME/dev" rather
# than "silently finds nothing". Do not rely on that; keep "*" generic.
# Memory directories are named by their path RELATIVE to this root, so both
# machines agree on `memory/robotics-armctl` even if the roots differ. Identical
# paths on both machines remain the recommended setup — this only means a machine
# that cannot manage it no longer silently loses its memory.
# If every machine keeps its workspace at ~/dev, the default row below is all you
# need. Add a machine-specific row only when one of them cannot — a Mac and a
# Linux box, for instance, cannot share an absolute path at all, because their
# home directories live under /Users and /home respectively. That case is handled:
# memory is named relative to the root, so both still agree.
